name: Tizanidine
metabolism: Extensively metabolized, chiefly by CYP1A2. Metabolites are not known to be active; elimination of drug-related material occurs mainly in urine and partly feces.
summary: Tizanidine is a centrally acting alpha-2 adrenergic agonist prescribed for spasticity. Its label warns of hypotension, bradycardia, and sedation.
dosageRemark: The label describes prescription dosing for spasticity: start at 2 mg every 6 to 8 hours as needed, with gradual increases under clinician supervision; the maximum total daily dose is 36 mg. These are prescription instructions, not recreational dose guidance.
generalRisks: The label warns of hypotension and syncope, bradycardia, sedation, liver injury, hallucinations, hypersensitivity, and withdrawal reactions. Fluvoxamine and ciprofloxacin are examples of strong CYP1A2 inhibitors and are contraindicated with tizanidine; moderate or weak CYP1A2 inhibitors should also be avoided because hypotension, bradycardia, or excessive drowsiness may occur. Alcohol and other CNS depressants add to sedation.
toxicities: The prescribing label warns of hepatocellular liver injury, hallucinations or psychotic-like symptoms, hypersensitivity including anaphylaxis/angioedema, and withdrawal reactions (rebound hypertension, tachycardia, hypertonia) after abrupt reduction or discontinuation.
Common adverse reactions in placebo-controlled studies included dry mouth, somnolence/sedation, asthenia, and dizziness; rates were dose related.
